items.cite: Carol A. Hess, *Sacred Passions: The Life and Music of Manuel de Falla* (Oxford University Press, 2005).
items.note: How do the life, the faith and the music fit together? A biography that draws on the Granada archive and sets Falla’s work in its historical and cultural context.

items.cite: Carol A. Hess, *Manuel de Falla and Modernism in Spain, 1898–1936* (University of Chicago Press, 2001).
items.note: What was Spanish modernism, and where did Falla stand in the political and cultural arguments before the Civil War? Hess approaches the period through his career.

items.cite: Manuel de Falla, *On Music and Musicians* (Marion Boyars, 1979), first published in Spanish as *Escritos sobre música y músicos* (1950).
items.note: What did Falla himself write about the composers and traditions he admired? His collected essays, in English translation.

items.cite: Archivo Manuel de Falla, Granada: chronology and life-and-work pages.
items.note: When and where did each work, journey and première happen? Year-by-year dates, with extracts from the letters preserved in the Granada archive.

items.cite: Jaime Pahissa, *Vida y obra de Manuel de Falla* (Ricordi Americana, 1947; second edition 1956).
items.note: What did Falla say about his own life in his last years? Pahissa, a Catalan composer in exile in Buenos Aires, made notes during a visit to Los Espinillos in 1944 for this early life.
